small_guidance:
- The conv kernel computes 64 IC × 9 (KH·KW) = 576 inner iterations per (oc_tile, sp_tile) with no K-tiling reuse — try restructuring inner loops so the IC loop becomes a tl.dot over a [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_IC] × [BLOCK_IC, BLOCK_SP] GEMM (IC=64 fits as a single K-tile). Sweep BLOCK_OC ∈ {32, 64}, BLOCK_SP ∈ {64, 128, 256} with num_warps ∈ {4, 8}, num_stages ∈ {2, 3} via triton.autotune.
- For GroupNorm, CPG·HW = 8 · 258·258 ≈ 533k; BLOCK_SIZE=1024 means ~520 iterations per program with reload of x in the second pass. Cache x in SRAM or use a single-pass Welford with online mean/var; alternatively raise BLOCK_SIZE to 2048 with num_warps=8 to reduce loop overhead.
- Hoist `c_in_group = idx // HW` and the gather of weight/bias outside the per-iteration scope by precomputing once per channel block (idx step is BLOCK_SIZE, so c_in_group changes slowly) — or split the second pass loop along channel dimension to load w/b once per channel.
large_guidance:
- Replace the gather-style ConvTranspose with an explicit GEMM: since stride=1, ConvTranspose2d with kernel 3 is equivalent to a regular conv2d with the spatially-flipped weight on a zero-padded (pad=KH-1) input. Implement as an im2col-tiled GEMM with tl.dot — one program per (N, OC tile, OH·OW tile), accumulating IC*KH*KW as the GEMM-K dimension. This unlocks tensor-core-class throughput vs. the current scalar FMA loop.
- Switch the layout to channels-last (NHWC) for the conv output so GroupNorm's reduction stride is contiguous along C-within-group; alternatively keep NCHW but fuse GroupNorm's first pass (sum, sumsq) into the conv epilogue by having each conv program atomically add partial stats to per-(N,G) accumulators, then run only a normalize-pass second kernel.
- Persistent GroupNorm: with N·G = 128·8 = 1024 programs and group_elems ≈ 533k, consider one program per (N, G) using a 2D tile that spans the full HW with multiple warps cooperatively reducing via tl.sum across a [CPG, BLOCK_HW] tile, avoiding the two full passes over global memory by keeping x resident in registers/SRAM across mean and normalize.
